title: ROB-G2-RQ: Grover search over robust shadow scores, O(2^{n/2} n^2 log^2 n) work, 3333/10000 online unflagged replacement tolerance (1/3 - 1/30000), O(n) copies and qubits

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-G2 algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^8), Q = 2^33 (n+4) copies, q = 24 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-24, threshold 6667/40000, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) has worst-case total work T(N,s) = O(2^{n/2} n^2 (log2 n)^2) in the challenge cost model (all classical bit operations, circuit generation, gates, measurements, initialisation, table construction, address charge ceil(log2(M+2)) = O(log n) per counted operation, where M = O(n^2) is the number of allocated bits plus qubits; each source copy costs n+1; proof.md Section 7: at most 3 repetitions of at most 0.785 * 2^{n/2} Grover iterations, each with an oracle of O(Q n log n) gates, plus O(n^3 log^2 n) for acquisition and label estimation), i.e. uniform envelope B_T(n) = 2^{n/2} n^2 (log2 n)^2, whose growth index is exactly 1. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every admissible strategy of the online unflagged replacement error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes).

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-G2 algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^8), Q = 2^33 (n+4) copies, q = 24 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-24, threshold 6667/40000, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) has worst-case peak classical space S_C(N,s) = O(n^2) bits (Q records of n+p+4 bits, the 2^24-entry cosine table and its constant-size construction workspace, an O(n log log n + n)-bit label-estimation and long-division workspace, the O(n)-bit search controller (K, k_G, counters, current constants, threshold, one stored gate description); explicitly S_C <= 2^33 (n+4)(n+p+4) + 27 * 2^24 + O(n log log n + n)), i.e. envelope B_C(n) = n^2, whose growth index is exactly 0. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every admissible strategy of the online unflagged replacement error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes).

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-G2 algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^8), Q = 2^33 (n+4) copies, q = 24 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-24, threshold 6667/40000, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) has worst-case peak quantum space S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits (acquisition: one held (n+1)-qubit source copy, one test control, O(n) adder ancillas and one fair-bit qubit, released after each copy; search: n candidate qubits, O(log n) qubits for the phase accumulator, table index, table word and score accumulator, O(n) comparator and diffusion ancillas), i.e. envelope B_Q(n) = n, whose growth index is exactly 0. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every admissible strategy of the online unflagged replacement error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes).

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-G2 algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^8), Q = 2^33 (n+4) copies, q = 24 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-24, threshold 6667/40000, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) acquires exactly Q(N,s) = 2^33 (n+4) <= 5 * 2^33 n copies on every execution branch (a deterministic count of all acquisitions, honest or replaced; every acquired copy yields one stored record and none is rejected; the acquisition phase is never restarted, and the search circuit is repeated at most three times on the same records, acquiring no copies; there are no aborts), so Q(N,s) = O(n), envelope B_samples(n) = n, whose growth index is exactly 0. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every admissible strategy of the online unflagged replacement error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes).

For the same ROB-G2 algorithm and configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 3333/10000, valid for every N >= 2 (no threshold), under the online unflagged replacement model stated in error_model and restated verbatim in proof.md Section 5.1: Q = 2^33 (n+4) is the actual count of acquired copies on every branch (every acquired copy yields one stored record), and almost surely at most floor(3333Q/10000) of them are replaced; each replacement bit is chosen before its acquisition, using N, s, the past classical transcript and a private quantum workspace, without access to the current honest draw or future protocol coins (every random outcome ROB-G2 obtains during acquisition, including its only fair bits m'_j, is obtained after the delivery of the copy it concerns, and its output phase starts after the last delivery); a replaced copy is any state on the n+1 input qubits, possibly entangled with the private workspace and other replaced copies; a non-replaced copy is a fresh rho_s tensor-independent of all prior systems; no replacement flag is supplied. For every N >= 2, every s in Z/NZ and every admissible strategy (including the one that replaces nothing, i.e. the clean problem), the output equals the entire s with probability at least 49/64 > 2/3 (proof.md Lemma R and Theorems 1 and 2), jointly with the four resource bounds above, which hold on every execution branch for every strategy. proof.md Proposition U (a proved remark, not part of this claim) shows that for even N and every epsilon > 1/3, no algorithm acquiring a fixed number Q > ln 6/(2(epsilon - 1/3)^2) of copies achieves success probability at least 2/3 for both secrets s and s + N/2 against every admissible strategy of this model; 3333/10000 = 1/3 - 1/30000.

structured.error_model: Online unflagged replacement model. Before each acquired copy, an adversary chooses a classical replacement bit using N, s, the past classical transcript and private quantum workspace, without access to the current fresh honest draw or future protocol coins. A non-replaced copy is a fresh rho_s tensor-independent of all prior systems; a replaced copy is any state on the same n+1 input qubits and may be entangled with private workspace and other replacements. No replacement flag is supplied. At termination Q is the actual count of all acquired copies, including rejects and discards, and at most floor(epsilon(n)*Q) were replaced almost surely for every admissible strategy; this is a promise, not postselection on budget fulfillment. Current honest labels cannot be inspected before deciding that call's type. All other gates and measurements are ideal. The probability is uniform over N,s and all such online strategies.
